title: 7.10 An 8-to-28GHz 8-Phase Clock Generator Using Dual-Feedback Ring Oscillator in 28nm CMOS
problem: Multi-phase clock generation for high-speed wireline transceivers (>224Gb/s PAM-4) requires low jitter and phase error across wide frequency range (8–28GHz); PLL-based approaches become costly at fT limits of 200–300GHz CMOS processes.
method: Dual-feedback ring oscillator: cascades DLL (delay-locked loop) with ring oscillator (RO) injection-locked by the DLL. DLL expands input clock to multiple phases; RO's autonomous feedback suppresses phase error and reduces jitter compared to standalone DLL while maintaining wide frequency tuning.

title: Security of Approximate Neural Networks against Power Side-channel Attacks
problem: Security implications of approximate computing in Artificial Neural Networks; understanding vulnerability to power side-channel attacks as approximate computing techniques (overclocking, voltage scaling, bitwise approximation) are deployed for energy reduction.
method: Evaluates power side-channel vulnerability of approximate ANN processing elements under three approximation scenarios: (1) overclocking, (2) voltage scaling, (3) circuit-level bitwise approximation. Performs weight extraction correlation power analysis (CPA) attacks; measures Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) degradation and Measurement-to-Disclosure (MTD) metric; analyzes trade-off via Security-Power-Delay (SPD) metric.

title: 37.6 A 22nm 60.81TFLOPS/W Diffusion Accelerator with Bandwidth-Aware Memory Partition and BL-Segmented Compute-in-Memory for Efficient Multi-Task Content Generation
problem: Existing CIM accelerators struggle with diffusion model efficiency due to: large operational intensity variation across layers creating dynamic bandwidth needs, 10x larger data storage than GANs/VAEs, system-level CIM efficiency degradation despite high macro efficiency, 59% CIM power consumed on data access, and 31% of operations spent on computationally-intensive multi-view/temporal attention.
method: 22nm CIM accelerator with bandwidth-aware memory partitioning to match dynamic layer requirements, BL-segmented compute-in-memory macros optimizing data reuse, and specialized operators for multi-view/temporal attention consistency in 3D/video tasks.

title: Tropical: Enhancing SLO Attainment in Disaggregated LLM Serving via SLO-Aware Multiplexing
problem: Disaggregated LLM serving isolates prefill and decode on separate workers to optimize one phase but creates high queuing delays; non-disaggregated serving reduces queuing but causes compute interference between phases, violating latency SLOs (TTFT, TPOT).
method: Tropical introduces SLO-aware multiplexing that dynamically balances prefill and decode execution on hybrid workers to leverage benefits of both disaggregated (low interference) and non-disaggregated (low queuing) architectures. Uses adaptive scheduling to minimize queuing delays while controlling interference, enabling simultaneous TTFT and TPOT SLO compliance.

title: BitMoD: Bit-serial Mixture-of-Datatype LLM Acceleration
problem: LLM deployment is constrained by large weight memory footprints; existing low-precision quantization schemes either sacrifice too much accuracy or lack hardware support for multiple heterogeneous data types simultaneously. Current accelerators cannot efficiently process mixed numerical formats (e.g., INT4, FP4, NF4) within a single design.
method: BitMoD is an algorithm-hardware co-design that introduces fine-grained per-group (128-weight) data-type adaptation, selecting from a set of carefully designed numerical types to minimize quantization error per group. On the hardware side, a bit-serial processing element natively handles multiple precisions by decomposing weights into bit-planes; a unified representation maps all data types to a common internal format, and a dedicated bit-serial dequantization unit rescales per-group partial sums with minimal overhead.

title: HPIM-NoC: A Priori-Knowledge-Based Optimization Framework for Heterogeneous PIM-Based NoCs
problem: Existing NoC simulators and architecture search frameworks are designed for homogeneous architectures and lack support for simulating and optimizing heterogeneous Processing-in-Memory (PIM) configurations with varied core capabilities.
method: HPIM-NoC implements a joint simulation and search framework supporting heterogeneous PIM cores with accurate latency modeling via NoC transmission delays and pipelines. It uses a three-stage heterogeneous search process based on priori knowledge with a customized simulated annealing algorithm, accelerated by precomputing core PPA metrics and reducing NoC simulation frequency, plus a customized layout algorithm.

title: 12.2 p-Circuits: Neither Digital Nor Analog
problem: Traditional analog and digital circuits present inherent trade-offs in power, area, and performance; a new computing paradigm is needed that combines benefits of both without requiring ADC/DAC conversions.
method: p-circuits introduce a probabilistic computing model where circuit inputs and outputs maintain digital-like interfaces (no ADC/DAC), but the output is a random binary variable whose probability P(B=1) is governed by an analog function A(inputs) that continuously varies between 0 and 1. This enables stochastic computation where probability encodes information.

title: Accelerating LLM Serving for Multi-turn Dialogues with Efficient Resource Management
problem: Current LLM serving frameworks recompute attention keys and values for all prior turns on each new query in a multi-turn dialogue, incurring substantial redundant compute overhead. Additionally, the long accumulated prompt lengths from multi-turn context cause head-of-line blocking under FCFS scheduling, underutilizing GPU resources.
method: The paper introduces efficient resource management for multi-turn LLM serving by preserving KV-cache state across turns to eliminate recomputation of prior-turn attention keys and values. A new scheduling policy replaces FCFS with a length-aware or priority-based scheduler that avoids head-of-line blocking by reordering or preempting long-prompt requests. KV-cache memory is managed dynamically to balance cache retention across concurrent multi-turn sessions, trading off memory capacity against recompute cost.

title: 19.9 An 11-to-16.4GHz, 3.4GHz/µs-Slope, 5.32GHz-Chirp-Bandwidth, 0.043%-RMS-Frequency-Error FMCW Digital PLL with Posterior-Segment DPD Featuring 5-Chirp-Cycle Convergence Time
problem: FMCW radars for autonomous driving and IoT require wide-bandwidth chirps with high linearity and fast convergence to multiple frequency bands; multi-vehicle interference and multi-mode operation demand rapid frequency-hopping and DPD convergence within single chirp bursts.
method: 11-to-16.4GHz digital PLL with posterior-segment digital predistortion (DPD) that converges in 5 chirp cycles, generating chirps with 3.4GHz/µs slope and 5.32GHz bandwidth, achieving 0.043% RMS frequency error despite nonlinearity.

title: LAD: Efficient Accelerator for Generative Inference of LLM with Locality Aware Decoding
problem: In LLM autoregressive decoding, the KV cache grows linearly with sequence length, and at lengths beyond 2048 tokens the attention mechanism's repeated read of the full KV cache becomes the dominant bottleneck, consuming over 50% of total inference time on GPU-based systems.
method: LAD (Locality Aware Decoding) is a dedicated ASIC accelerator that exploits numerical locality in attention scores across consecutive decoding steps. The key insight is that when an attention score at a specific sequence position remains approximately constant across several consecutive decoding steps, the corresponding key and value vectors need not be re-fetched at every step. LAD implements a locality detection engine that identifies stable-score positions and caches their contribution, dramatically reducing KV cache access frequency while maintaining decoding accuracy. The hardware includes specialized attention decoding units paired with on-chip score history buffers to track and exploit inter-step score locality.

title: A 100Gbaud 4Vppd Distributed Linear Driver with Cross-Folded Transmission Lines and Cross-Coupled Gm Cells for Built-in 5-Tap FFE in 0.13µm SiGe BiCMOS
problem: Linear pluggable optics (LPO) drivers must provide large output swing (high extinction ratio), high gain, and wide bandwidth simultaneously for short-reach fiber optics; conventional distributed amplifiers lack equalization, while transmission-line (TL) based FFE designs cannot achieve both high gain and large swing.
method: A distributed linear driver using cross-folded transmission lines and cross-coupled Gm cells that achieves both high gain and large output swing (4 Vppd). The transmission lines provide dual functionality: (1) passive frequency-response shaping for bandwidth extension, and (2) passive delay-line FFE implementation with 5 programmable taps for equalization.

title: 30.3 A 24Gb 42.5Gb/s GDDR7 DRAM with Low-Power WCK Distribution, an RC-Optimized Dual-Emphasis TX, and Voltage/Time-Margin-Enhanced Power Reduction
problem: GDDR7 DRAM must achieve 42.5Gb/s data rates while managing power consumption and thermal throttling in high-performance AI systems requiring extensive datasets and GPU processing.
method: The design introduces low-power write-clock (WCK) distribution, an RC-optimized dual-emphasis transmitter (TX), and voltage/time-margin-enhanced techniques to reduce power while maintaining high bandwidth PAM3 signaling at 42.5Gb/s.

title: 14.1 A 22nm 104.5TOPS/W µ-NMC-Δ-IMC Heterogeneous STT-MRAM CIM Macro for Noise-Tolerant Bayesian Neural Networks
problem: Image recognition under noise (environmental interference) degrades accuracy in CNNs and ViTs. Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) offer better noise tolerance but implementing them in edge hardware requires efficient in-memory computing while handling μ-weight (mean) and Δ-weight (deviation) representations.
method: Heterogeneous STT-MRAM CIM macro combining μ-NMC (mean computation) and Δ-IMC (deviation in-memory compute) paths, processing mean and delta weight components separately with optimized circuitry for each. Leverages STT-MRAM for efficient weight storage.

title: Instruction-Aware Cooperative TLB and Cache Replacement Policies
problem: Modern server and data center applications have large instruction footprints that cause frequent instruction-side TLB and cache misses, with instruction TLB (iTLB) misses being particularly harmful because they cause pipeline stalls that block forward progress. Existing TLB and cache replacement policies treat instruction and data streams equivalently and do not account for the criticality of instruction accesses.
method: The paper proposes instruction-aware cooperative replacement policies that distinguish instruction accesses from data accesses in both the TLB and cache. The cooperative approach coordinates eviction decisions between the iTLB and the instruction cache (iCache), so that evicting a page from the iTLB also triggers or informs iCache eviction decisions and vice versa, reducing redundant refills. Replacement decisions are guided by instruction-access frequency and recency, with policy cooperation preventing the two structures from working at cross-purposes during instruction working set thrashing.

title: Cascade: A Dependency-aware Efficient Training Framework for Temporal Graph Neural Network
problem: TGNN training is severely constrained by temporal dependencies between input events: large batches improve parallelism but cause infrequent node memory updates leading to stale information and accuracy degradation, forcing small-batch training with high latency and underutilized hardware.
method: Cascade uses a topology-aware scheduler that packs as many spatially-independent events as possible into the same batch, then leverages inter-node memory similarity to identify 'stabilized' nodes whose memories have converged sufficiently to safely break temporal dependencies. This similarity-based dependency breaking allows temporally-independent events to be included in larger batches. An adaptive update frequency mechanism based on runtime feedback further reduces redundant memory updates, achieving 2.3x average (up to 5.1x) speedup without accuracy loss.

title: Memory: Almost The Only Thing That Matters : A revolution in memory architecture for the data center
problem: Data center performance bottleneck has shifted from computation to memory bandwidth and latency; traditional DRAM hierarchies and interconnects cannot keep pace with compute acceleration.
method: The work proposes architectural innovations in memory hierarchy, bandwidth, and interconnect design. Likely includes advanced memory technologies (HBM, 3D stacking), new interconnect protocols, and memory-compute co-design.
